promise: A query term matches a host only where the host's name actually holds it: inside one label, typed straight through the separators, or read off the label initials.
why: Subsequence over a whole name is too generous once names carry six labels. On a fleet named role.env.product.region.example.com, 'qa' took its q from the role and its a from a label three along, so three terms that named one host returned every host in the product and typing more never narrowed. The highlight had the same bug and hid it: both characters landed under ranges other terms had already painted, so a term matching invisibly looked exactly like a term matching nothing.
command: scripts/test.sh --filter RoamingTokenSearchTests --filter AnchoredTokenTests --filter HighlightAgreesWithScoreTests 2>&1 | grep -qE 'Executed [1-9][0-9]* tests, with 0 failures'
